steps.action: Pose the question of wave dissipation and the forcing of setup and runup on La Saline fringing reef, aiming at transfer functions for coastal management.
steps.quote: this study addresses the question of wave dissipation on La Saline (La Réunion island) fringing reef

steps.action: Design and deploy a cross-shore transect with a reef-slope pressure sensor plus current profiler and a reef-flat pressure sensor for 53 days.
steps.quote: was deployed for 53 days across La Saline reef from 13-Mar-2017 to 05-May-2017

steps.action: Correct pressure records for atmospheric and non-hydrostatic effects, low-pass filter for depth, and compute GW, IG and VLF spectra and wave parameters by FFT.
steps.quote: The residual high frequency signal was kept for spectral analysis

steps.action: Estimate reef-flat setup and the relative vertical offset of the sensors from a regression of depth difference on reef-slope wave height and time (Vetter et al. 2010), and tie sensors to the IGN89 datum with LIDAR/hyperspectral bathymetry.
steps.quote: allowing for an accurate estimate of the vertical position of the RS sensor

steps.action: Compare measured reef-slope wave height, period and direction with WaveWatch III hindcasts at an offshore node.
steps.quote: The linear fit between the modeled and observed data at the reef slope is quite good

steps.action: Identify three swell events (P1, P2 moderate; P3 strong) under different tidal ranges and still water levels as periods of interest.
steps.quote: Three periods of interest were identified corresponding to two moderate swell events marked P1 and P2 and a stronger event marked P3

steps.action: Configure a 1-D XBeach surfbeat model on a smoothed cross-shore bathymetric profile, forced by measured reef-slope spectra and tide, justified by cited validations.
steps.quote: Here, the model was run in XBSB mode over a 1-D domain with a primary focus on cross-reef wave processes.

steps.action: Run a mesh convergence test over several resolutions, leading to a 10 m mesh.
steps.quote: a mesh convergence test was performed

steps.action: Calibrate the wave friction coefficient fw and the Manning-based bed friction cf against reef-flat observations (fw = 0.3, n = 0.02), and choose the Roelvink and Brøker breaking formulation.
steps.quote: The optimal values for the configuration of the XBeach model were found to be

steps.action: Describe the measured spectra: GW nearly removed across the reef, IG double peak, VLF peak near 18.5 min on the reef flat.
steps.quote: The reef clearly acts as a low-pass filter maintaining energy in the IG band on the reef flat.

steps.action: Compare the observed VLF peak period with the first seiche mode period computed from reef width and depth.
steps.quote: This value is of the same order of magnitude to the first seiche mode period of 15 min

steps.action: Quantify 97% mean GW attenuation varying with tide, and IG and VLF amplification on the reef flat with tidal modulation and a threshold near 2.5 m incident height.
steps.quote: Wave attenuation varied between 92% and 98% from high tide to low tide respectively

steps.action: Fit the Lentz et al. (2016) analytic decay equation to reef-flat GW height versus depth plus setup, with gamma fixed at 0.55, giving fw = 0.2.
steps.quote: The wave height variability described by Equation 6 is well-reproduced for a wave

steps.action: Describe setup (0.08 to 0.86 m, mean 18% of incident height), higher at low tide and in antiphase with tide.
steps.quote: The setup variations are in antiphase with the tidal signal

steps.action: Compare modeled and measured GW, IG, VLF and setup at both stations: good for GW, IG and setup; VLF poorly reproduced (R2 = 0.41); setup underestimated in P3.
steps.quote: High correlations indicate that the model configuration is well adapted the prediction of

steps.action: Use the validated model to estimate unmeasured runup (R2%) and the relative contributions of tide, setup, GW, IG and VLF to shoreline water level.
steps.quote: the XBeach model is used to estimate runup

steps.action: Fit multilinear transfer functions from offshore wave height, period or power and water level to reef-flat IG, VLF, setup and runup.
steps.quote: Furthermore, 79% of the runup is explained by incident wave conditions and 21% by tidal fluctuations.

steps.action: Set the findings against other reefs: open-ocean forcing, fw within published ranges, and the Lentz analytical model extended to low water levels.
steps.quote: The analytical model (Lentz et al., 2016) is validated in the case of the La Saline fringing reef

steps.action: Note that the expected depth dependence of the VLF period is not observed and the period differs from the seiche estimate.
steps.quote: The expected variation of the mean period of VLF waves with the water depth is not observed

steps.action: Compare setup dependence on wave height and tide with Vetter et al. (2010) and other studies.
steps.quote: This corroborates the high correlation between setup and incident wave heights observed in a shore-attached fringing reef by Vetter et al. (2010).

steps.action: Compare the XBeach-calibrated fw = 0.3 with the analytically inferred fw = 0.2 and attribute the gap to numerical difficulty in resolving bottom friction.
steps.quote: Such small differences between both values can find some explanation in the difficulty to numerically resolve bottom friction

steps.action: After the poor VLF prediction, test 60 and 180 min boundary-forcing intervals; VLF heights do not improve and noise increases, so 10 min is kept.
steps.quote: modifications to allow for a delay of 60 min or 180 min between each forcing do not improve VLF height prediction

steps.action: Offer cited explanations for setup underestimation in P3: linear wave theory radiation stress (Buckley et al. 2015) and missing 3D current shear (Guérin et al. 2018).
steps.quote: Buckley et al. (2015) give a first possible explanation for this using laboratory experiments.

steps.action: Compare the runup transfer function with BEWARE (XBNH idealized-reef database, Pearson et al. 2017) for a similar reef geometry.
steps.quote: Comparison shows a good match between both.

steps.action: Extrapolate the transfer functions to a 50 cm sea-level rise scenario (RCP4.5) to project increases in IG height and runup.
steps.quote: Extrapolating from the proposed transfer functions (cf. Table 3) IG significant wave height would increase by 9 cm, and beach runup by 30 cm.

steps.action: Keep the transfer functions and the setup-dominated, tide-modulated account of reef hydrodynamics.
steps.quote: The present study proposes simple-to-use transfer functions to linearly combine contributors such as the water level and incident wave

tree.answer: Wave dissipation, setup and runup over a fringing reef under Southern Ocean swell
Wave heights and setup measured directly; runup not measured, estimated with a calibrated model
Transfer functions linking incident waves and tide to setup and runup
No rival hypotheses for the main claim; cited explanations only for the setup bias in P3
Conditions found: natural swell events P1-P3 and tidal cycles during a 53-day deployment

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Nature repeats swell events and semidiurnal tides, sampled over 53 days
Partly: mesh convergence, forcing-interval test, BEWARE comparison; VLF not reproduced; no held-out test of the transfer functions
Transfer functions kept within the sampled range (Hs up to about 4.5 m)

end.claim: At La Saline, setup and runup are predicted by linear transfer functions of offshore wave height and water level: setup 98% wave-driven and 2% tide-driven, runup 79% and 21%, with both in antiphase with the tide; the functions are valid for Hs up to about 4.5 m and reef-crest depths up to 1.5 m.

decisive_move.sentence: The multilinear fit of measured setup and model-estimated runup against offshore wave height and water level produces the transfer functions and variance partitions that make up the headline claim.

gates.evidence: The deployment was designed to describe wave transformation, not to test a stated hypothesis (p. 3). Model validation against reef-flat data could fail, and it did fail for VLF (p. 14). The transfer functions are fitted to the same data and model output, with no held-out test; the BEWARE comparison is a post hoc consistency check (p. 19). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen; fw and cf were calibrated to the data (p. 9).

imports.item: Fast Fourier Transform with Hamming windowing and second-order Butterworth low-pass filter
Depth-dependent Manning formulation for the bed friction coefficient
Rayleigh distribution assumption to convert HRMS to Hs
Multiple linear regression for transfer functions and variance partitioning

novelty_claims.quote: the present study completes the validation, by adding much data in the polynomial section of the curve, at low water levels

limits: Runup was never measured; every runup claim rests on the XBeach model calibrated on the same reef-flat data used to validate it, with no independent hold-out (inference). The friction coefficients were tuned to the observations, so the good validation statistics are partly built in. Setup is underestimated by up to 25% in P3, and the authors state the maximum runup may therefore be underestimated. VLF waves are poorly reproduced (R2 = 0.41). Only one cross-shore transect with two stations was used, and the results are stated to be site-specific. The sea-level-rise projections extrapolate the transfer functions beyond the calibrated water levels (inference). The process records one revised modelling attempt (forcing interval, p. 18); other tuning iterations are not reported. Sub-claims: fw = 0.2 from the Lentz equation (estimate_with_resolution, no uncertainty given); low-pass filtering and 97% GW attenuation (regularity_in_range); model capability for GW, IG and setup (capability_characterized, failing for VLF).

disagreements.target: Lentz et al. (2016), platform reef analysis of wave decay
disagreements.support: On a fringing reef the setup is of the same order as the water depth, so it must be included in the depth used in the decay equation; the low-water data extend Lentz's validation.
disagreements.quote: it is not clear if setup plays a major role in GW height over the reef flat

disagreements.quote: suggest that idealized configurations of reef systems with good friction parameterization should be enough to reproduce the water level in the reef flat

disagreements.target: Expected depth dependence of the reef-flat seiche (first seiche mode) period
disagreements.support: The observed VLF mean period of 18 min differs from the 15 min seiche estimate and does not vary with water depth.
